newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, volatile on crop talk.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, volatile on crop talk.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed mixed but well above the session lows on a late recovery triggered by talk that more wheat than expected may have been lost during the freeze in the Plains over the April 12-13 weekend, traders said.
"Commercials pushed it down on the open and through the course of the day, commercials became buyers," a trader said.

Private crop consultant Dale Fain said Oklahoma may struggle to produce 100 million bushels of hard red winter wheat this year following recent freeze and disease damage, around half the total that might otherwise have been expected.
Fain said the crop potential in Kansas and Texas may also have been halved although he emphasized his information on those states was less extensive.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed 2-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 6-1/2 cents lower, with May up 2-1/2 at $4.97 a bushel. July was down 1/2 cent at $4.79.
Volume was estimated at 50.065 million bushels, below the 66.925 million bushels traded Monday.
